metadata.context_method: Oracle context around a deterministic gold class; no retrieved or shuffled conditions.
metadata.oracle_centre_policy: deepest graph-minimal annotated class, class ID tie-break; all gold types retained for scoring

prompt:
List valid entity-type labels, most specific first, then broader valid types. Use concise labels, not entity names or descriptions. Include only evidence-supported types; do not repeat labels or pad the list.

The taxonomy context contains only direct child classes of an omitted target type. Child classes are narrower than the omitted target and can help indicate its specificity boundary. They are structural clues, not answer options. Do not predict a child merely because it is listed; use a narrower child only when the entity description independently supports it.

Return JSON only in exactly this form:
{"types": ["type 1", "type 2", "..."]}

Example:

Entity: Katsuhiro Harada
Description: Japanese video game producer

Taxonomy context:
- Direct child classes: None

Answer:
{"types": ["video game producer", "producer", "media professional", "professional", "worker", "person", "person or organization", "corporate body", "object", "entity"]}

Now classify:

Entity: William Jennings Miller
Description: U.S. Representative from Connecticut (1899-1950)

Taxonomy context:
- Direct child classes: administrative act, punishment, court decision

Answer:
response: {"types": ["U.S. Representative", "representative", "politician", "government figure", "public official", "official", "worker", "person", "person or organization", "corporate body", "organization", "institution", "legal body", "jurisdictional body", "organization or corporate body", "corporate entity", "object", "entity", "thing", "existent", "unit of matter", "physical object", "object or widget"]}
